question: is the verdict fragility a 4-bit quantisation artefact
design: Qwen3-30B-A3B, SAME export at two precisions. Same architecture, tokenizer, pipeline class (LLMPipeline), flattened prompt shape, and speculative decoding OFF on both. Only weight precision varies.
gauntlet: datamark PINNED; three meaning-preserving perturbations of the retrieved text

decides.int4 moves, int8 steady: quantisation - actionable by us and useful upstream
decides.both move: architecture or model family, not precision
decides.neither moves: fragility is specific to the Qwen3.6-35B export

Qwen3-30B-A3B int8.why_not: NOT MEASURABLE ON THIS HARDWARE. Loaded successfully in a clean process (561s vs int4's 40s) and then ran 43+ minutes without completing a single variant that takes 52s on int4 - a ~50x slowdown with system memory pinned at 30.6-31.2 GB of 31.32. That is continuous paging, not slow inference. Killed rather than babysat. Any number taken under that pressure would be confounded by the pressure.
Qwen3-30B-A3B int8.first_attempt_error: In the combined process it failed outright: '[CL ext] Can not allocate 201326592 bytes for USM Host' - OpenVINO had not released the int4 arm's device memory. One model per process is mandatory for these.

verdict: UNRESOLVED, and unresolvable on this box. int4 is fragile on BOTH mixture-of-experts models tested (Qwen3.6-35B: ag-noegress-01 moved; Qwen3-30B: ag-empty-01 moved), while the dense Qwen3-14B int4 does not move at all. The int8 arm that would separate '4-bit compression' from 'mixture-of-experts architecture' cannot be run here: it needs more RAM than this machine has to spare, and that is a hardware decision, not a measurement one.
what_would_settle_it: the same gauntlet on Qwen3-30B-A3B int8 on a machine with >=48 GB, or
an int8 export of a SMALLER mixture-of-experts model that fits with headroom, or
a dense model at int4 other than the 14B, to test whether density rather than precision is what protects it
